thread:
anya: Quick sync 11 need final decision on public comms for last week's API incident: (1) short status page copy, (2) whether we publish the RCA or provide on-request only, (3) redaction rules for on-request RCAs. Aim: lock by EOD Thu so CS can notify affected customers.

olivia: paste the current draft status blurb? i have wording tweaks.

anya: current draft below:
```
Status: Incident resolved
Summary: We experienced elevated API error rates between 2026-03-18 02:10 UTC and 2026-03-18 03:45 UTC due to a degraded autoscaling path that prevented new worker allocations. Impact: a subset of request types returned 500 errors or timed out. Mitigation: we rolled forward a fix and resumed normal autoscaling. Customers may see elevated latency for a short window after the rollback while caches warmed.
Next steps: a full post-incident summary and remediation timeline will be provided.
```

olivia: suggested edits: avoid internal terms like "autoscaling path" and "rolled forward". replace with simpler phrasing: "capacity provisioning issue" and "deployed a targeted configuration rollback". also specify impacted request types if we can: "requests with large payloads or client-side streaming"?

mike: +1 on simpler language. public page should be concise. also don't call out internal mechanisms beyond "capacity provisioning".

sam: for customer-facing availability of the RCA, legal prefers "available on request for affected customers" rather than fully public, especially since we may reference traces.

nina: legal input: we can publish a high-level summary. Anything containing logs/traces or customer identifiers must be redacted. On-request RCAs should follow a redaction checklist; CS needs to collect affected-customer confirmation and sign an NDA for access to sensitive traces unless heavily redacted.

olivia: here's a tightened public blurb proposal:
```
Status: Resolved
Summary: Between 02:1003:45 UTC on 2026-03-18, certain API requests experienced increased errors due to a capacity provisioning failure. We deployed a targeted configuration rollback; services have returned to normal. Affected customers may request a detailed incident summary from support.
```

anya: that looks good. prefer "detailed incident summary" rather than "RCA" on the public page.

mike: my recommendation: publish only the high-level summary publicly. do not publish full RCA. infra to prepare a redacted, shareable RCA for on-request delivery. owner: mike. timeline: redaction draft by Fri EOD, legal sign-off by Mon.

sam: support flow: when customer requests the detailed summary, CS will open an infra-redaction ticket with the incident id and customer id. need a template of what we include (high-level timeline, root cause, mitigations, and redaction notes). i'll draft the CS template by Thu.

nina: redaction checklist: remove customer IDs, IPs, raw span traces, S3 keys, internal hostnames; replace with hashed identifiers when useful; annotate any retained metrics with sampling/aggregation details. we should also include a short cover note describing redaction steps performed.

anya: note: this is the third scaling-related incident in 9 months. add recurring-incident action item in the postmortem tracker: deep RCA into autoscaling behavior, update runbooks, add e2e load tests, and consider capacity-provisioning guardrails.

mike: i'll open a remediation epic and link it in the postmortem. owner: infra-runtime. milestones: proposal by 2026-04-08, implementation plan by 2026-05-01.

olivia: action items i'll capture (own statuspage copy):
1) Finalize public status blurb 1 owner: olivia 1 due: Thu EOD
2) CS template for on-request incident summaries 1 owner: sam 1 due: Thu EOD
3) Draft RCA redaction + legal review 1 owners: mike, nina 1 draft due: Fri EOD, sign-off: Mon
4) Open remediation epic for recurring scaling incidents 1 owner: mike 1 create by Mon, proposals by 2026-04-08

anya: scheduling check 1 propose 30m sync Fri 10:00 UTC to confirm redaction progress and CS template. who can make it?

mike: i can.

olivia: me too.

sam: yes.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-18-API-123 closed by anya. Postmortem created: https://redwood.company/postmortems/2026-03-18-API-123

anya: thanks all. if no further comments i'll publish olivia's status blurb after legal confirms the redaction approach. :thumbsup:

mike: no objections from infra.

nina: will review redaction checklist Thu morning.

anya: closing thread, will update tracker with owners.
